title: Paint - RGBA layer, shared brush engine, alpha brush pack
description:
New rail tool in the History workspace, image mode: paint colour onto the entry. Deliberately simple - brush, eraser with the opacity slider we already ship for masking, a colour picker, Clear paint, Apply paint.

Why it earns its place (user's reasoning): a scribble is an INPUT to the models, not decoration. Paint a rough shape, then mask it and run detail over it - the model gets a shape reference plus the prompt instead of the prompt alone. It is the cheapest way to say 'put something roughly here, roughly this colour, roughly this big'.

Most of the surface already exists. MPI-371 extracted the shared MpiMaskStrip (brush/eraser pair, size, opacity) as a mountable strip - reuse it rather than authoring a second one. What is genuinely new is a COLOUR layer on MpiCanvas: MaskManager's layers are binary alpha (manualCanvas / subtractCanvas / autoPickMasks), so paint needs its own RGBA layer that composites over the image without polluting the mask layers - the two must stay independent, because the whole point is painting first and MASKING the paint afterwards.

Apply must not round-trip a 4K image as base64. Follow the MPI-362 precedent: send the paint layer to the server and let Sharp flatten it onto the source, appending one new history entry (new or extended route).

BLAST RADIUS: new MpiToolOptionsPaint (CSS in js/shell/preloadStyles.js, props in js/components/types.js), MpiHistoryTools rail entry, MpiCanvas + a PaintManager beside MaskManager, MpiCanvasViewer plumbing (per-entry load/clear, the same way masks are handled), the server flatten route, docs/masking.md or a new docs/painting.md.

--- UNDO CONTRACT (MPI-376 shipped 2026-07-29) ---
MpiCanvas now owns a shared UndoStack and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z work on the mask layers. Any mutation of manualCanvas / subtractCanvas this card adds MUST record an undo entry or it silently punches a hole in Ctrl+Z. Layer-wide one-shot op -> mask._recordUndo() before mutating (after any early-return guard). Gesture -> undo.begin(mask.undoLayers()) at the start, undo.commit(mask.takeStrokeBox()) at the end, undo.abort() if nothing changed. READ docs/masking-undo.md FIRST.
Specific to this card: UndoStack is deliberately layer-agnostic (an entry is a list of rect patches over arbitrary 2D contexts), so the paint RGBA layer plugs into the SAME stack. Do not grow a second one - that was the whole reason undo was built before paint.

--- RE-SCOPED 2026-08-01 by the MPI-424 brainstorm ---
This card now owns the BRUSH ENGINE, not just a paint tool. Mask Brush and Paint Brush are one engine with two destinations - binary mask layers, or the new RGBA paint layer - so the extraction happens here and both mounts come out of it. The Paint group also holds Shapes, but that gizmo belongs to MPI-368.
ALSO ABSORBED HERE: the alpha brush pack (ten brush textures, originally MPI-401). It moved off MPI-382 when Adjust stopped being a strip control; with one shared engine, both the mask brush and the paint brush get the textures in a single pass.
Sequenced FOURTH - after the gizmo, so the Paint group is complete in one stretch.

--- RESEQUENCED THIRD 2026-08-03 (user) ---
Swapped ahead of MPI-368 (Shapes). The shape gizmo is ONE geometry with TWO destinations and this card builds the second one, so Paint has to exist first or MPI-368 can only ship half of itself. This card is therefore the next in the MPI-424 order. Rationale: tasks/MPI-424/brief.md under the Order table.

--- SCOPED + DECIDED 2026-08-03 (user, at planning) ---
ALPHA BRUSH PACK SPLIT OUT to MPI-435. It has no source assets (nothing brush-textured exists in the repo) and only the paint layer + tool + Apply + the shared brush plumbing unblock MPI-368. Keeping the pack here would have made the umbrella hostage to getting ten textures made. MPI-435 is blocked on this card, which owns the dab helper it parameterises.

EXTRACTION = THE DAB, NOT A CLASS. Pull out one shared stampDab(ctx, x, y, r, op, style) plus dab interpolation along a stroke. MaskManager keeps its two-layer logic (manual + subtract), PaintManager gets its one-layer logic; both call the same stamp. A full BrushEngine class was rejected: it rewrites a working shared primitive and every call site in InputController, MpiCanvas and the undo wiring for no behaviour the small version does not deliver. The promise -- one engine, two destinations -- is kept because MPI-435 lands textures in that ONE function and both brushes get them.

PAINT PERSISTS PER ENTRY, like masks: temp PNG keyed by (project, group, item), reloaded on return. The card demanded this be decided rather than accidental. Discard-on-exit was rejected because the headline flow is paint -> mask -> detail, which SPANS a tool switch; it would break at step one.

NOT IN THIS CARD: brush textures (MPI-435), the shape gizmo (MPI-368, which now follows this card and needs the RGBA layer this one builds).
acceptance: Paint tool available in the rail for image entries in the History workspace
Brush, eraser with opacity, colour picker, Clear paint and Apply paint all work
The paint layer is independent of the mask layers - painting then masking the painted area works, and neither wipes the other
Apply appends ONE new history entry, flattened server-side, no base64 round-trip of a full-res image
Switching entries or leaving the tool has defined paint behaviour (persist per entry like masks, or discard) - decided, not accidental
Undo works on paint strokes (MPI-376 - do not ship paint with no undo)
Every new mask/paint layer mutation records an UndoStack entry (docs/masking-undo.md) - an unwired mutation is a silent hole in Ctrl+Z
